raw_response:
I am getting old, and with only 8 mu and two people at home, I cannot spread myself too thin. Maize is still the main crop for steady grain and feed, but I will keep some mungbean because it needs less fertilizer and less water, and if maize price is not good, mungbean can still bring some cash. I do things the old way that I know. For maize, I will put more land because it is safer for yield, about 5 mu. For mungbean, I will keep 3 mu. I have a well, but pumping costs money, so I will not water too many times unless the sky stays dry. I do not read those technical papers, I look at the soil, the seedlings, and what people nearby are doing. If maize comes up weak or yellow, I add a bit more fertilizer. Mungbean I keep lighter, because if I spend too much on it, the money may not come back.
